headline: High: shared writable server-side state plus unsandboxed Langflow Python creates dangerous cross-agent conflict and cascading-error paths; Flowise adds broad egress and file access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and both expose server-side files/workspaces. Flowise can ingest uploaded files and Langflow can chain tools and Python code, so attacker-controlled content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. This is not proven to be a direct default bridge, but the shared file surfaces make injection plausible.
conditions: IF either agent writes untrusted content into a shared file path
IF the other agent parses that file as prompts or tool instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct directories
Disable file-based prompt ingestion for both flows
Add a manual review step before any file is re-used as instructions
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and secrets, and both have broad network egress. Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials; Langflow stores per-flow credentials and can run arbitrary HTTP services. In a shared workspace, sensitive inputs or credentials can leak through files or outbound calls, though the profiles do not prove uncontrolled exfiltration by default.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in a shared server filesystem
IF either flow sends file contents to an external model provider or HTTP service
mitigations: Store secrets in separate vaults per agent
Restrict outbound domains for both agents
Avoid placing sensitive files in shared upload directories
Rotate any credentials used in shared flows
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write to the same server-side storage model, and both support multiple instances with shared state via server datastore/stores. Langflow also runs unsandboxed Python by default, increasing the chance of concurrent mutation or overwrite. This matches the rubric’s dangerous write-conflict pattern.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory or datastore
IF concurrent runs modify the same flow artifacts or cached state
mitigations: Assign separate storage roots per agent
Serialize writes with an external lock
Disable concurrent edits on shared artifacts
Snapshot state before running either agent
requires-engineering: add transactional storage or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Both are graph-based orchestration systems that chain tools and agents. Flowise can emit outputs from tools-as-nodes, and Langflow can chain multiple agents with unsandboxed Python. If one agent’s output is fed into the other without verification, errors or fabricated facts can cascade into downstream actions or rendered results.
conditions: IF Flowise outputs are consumed by Langflow without validation
IF Langflow uses those outputs to trigger tools or Python components
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require citations or schema checks on exchanged outputs
Disable automatic handoff between flows
Log and review any tool-triggering outputs
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Langflow explicitly stores per-flow credentials and runs unsandboxed Python by default while Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so I cannot claim a specific legal mismatch; however, differing retention and secret-handling practices create a plausible compliance gap.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in either agent’s server-side state
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Document retention settings for both systems
Avoid storing regulated data in flow state
Review where credentials are persisted
Align deletion procedures across both deployments
requires-engineering: perform a residency and certification review
